changes.evidence: Coverage, WASSCE 4 (partial): the electronic/digital balance is not named in any covers line.
changes.change: Added electronic (digital) balances to the list of balances.

changes.evidence: Coverage, WASSCE 5 and 5(a) (partial): the concept of time as the interval between physical events is not named.
changes.change: Added time as the interval between physical events.

changes.evidence: Coverage, WASSCE 15 and 15(b), UTME 6 and 6 definitions (partial): no covers line defines energy as the capacity to do work.
changes.change: Added energy as the capacity to do work at the head of the covers line.

changes.evidence: Coverage, WASSCE 14(b) note: biomass is in the WAEC note but not the covers line.
changes.change: Added biomass to the renewable sources.

changes.evidence: Coverage, WASSCE 16 and 16(b) (partial): change of colour and change in chemical properties are not named; scheme of work SS2 T1 W1 (partial): sources and uses of heat are not named.
changes.change: Added sources and uses of heat, and change of colour and change in chemical properties to the effects of heat.

changes.evidence: Coverage, WASSCE 25(2) and 25(2)(a) (partial): the alkaline-cadmium cell is not named; UTME 30 and 30(iii) (partial): lithium and mercury-cadmium cells are not named.
changes.change: Added alkaline-cadmium accumulators and lithium and mercury-cadmium cells, and named NiFe.

changes.evidence: Coverage, UTME 30 and 30(vi) (partial): the efficiency of a cell is not named.
changes.change: Added the efficiency of a cell.

changes.evidence: Coverage, scheme of work SS3 T1 W5 (partial): osmosis is not named anywhere.
changes.change: Added osmosis to the evidence that matter is made of particles.

changes.evidence: Coverage, scheme of work SS3 T2 W5 (partial): the need for machines and their repairs and maintenance are not named.
changes.change: Added why machines are needed and the care and maintenance of machines.

changes.evidence: Coverage, scheme of work SS3 T2 W6 (partial): the component parts of a rocket and a satellite are not named.
changes.change: Added the parts of a rocket and of a satellite and what each does.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, opus finding (missing, heat-transfer.radiation): detecting radiant heat (thermopile, Leslie cube) is named nowhere; UTME 2019 Q4 disagreement (sonnet temperature.thermometers, opus heat-transfer.radiation).
changes.change: Named the Leslie cube and detecting radiant heat with the thermopile.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME 2019 Q4 disagreement, 'Radiant heat can only be measured with a' (thermopile), split between temperature.thermometers and heat-transfer.radiation.
changes.change: Both covers lines now say: an instrument that detects radiant heat, such as the thermopile, goes to heat-transfer.radiation; a thermometer that measures the temperature of a body, including the thermocouple and pyrometer, goes to temperature.thermometers.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME 2021 Q24 disagreement (object distance for a same-size real image, sonnet lenses.formula, opus lenses.images); opus finding (overlap, lenses.images): say which wins when no working is needed.
changes.change: Both covers lines now say: a question answered from the standard image positions, such as an object at 2F for a same-size image, goes to lenses.images even when f is given and a distance is asked; one that needs the lens formula or a worked magnification goes to lenses.formula.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, sonnet finding (overlap, atom.photoelectric / atom.energy-levels) and opus finding (overlap, atom.energy-levels): a bare E = hc/lambda calculation set as light on a metal is routed to atom.photoelectric by a rule that contradicts how_to_use.
changes.change: Replaced the energy-levels rule: photon energy from E = hf or hc/lambda, with no work function, threshold or stopping potential needed, goes to atom.energy-levels whatever the setting; anything needing the photoelectric equation goes to atom.photoelectric. Added the mirror rule to atom.photoelectric.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, sonnet finding (overlap, expansion.solids / expansion.liquids): a question asking which expansivity does not apply to solids (apparent expansivity) needs both.
changes.change: expansion.liquids now names comparisons of solid and liquid expansivities; both covers lines say such a comparison goes to expansion.liquids.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, sonnet finding (overlap, vectors.resolution / equilibrium.coplanar): a single rope at an angle pulling a body along a smooth surface falls between the two.
changes.change: Both covers lines now say: a single force at an angle with nothing to balance it, where its component along the surface is asked, goes to vectors.resolution; the acceleration or work that follows goes to newtons-laws.second-law or energy.work.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, opus finding (overlap, sound.characteristics): how length, tension and thickness of a string set its pitch fits both.
changes.change: sound.strings now names how length, tension and mass per unit length set a string's frequency and pitch; both covers lines send that question to sound.strings and pitch in general to sound.characteristics.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, opus finding (missing, atom.models): Dalton's atomic theory and general statements about atoms of elements have no named home and split between atom.models and matter.particles.
changes.change: Added Dalton's atomic theory and general statements about the atoms of an element to atom.models, and a rule in matter.particles sending them there.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, opus finding (missing, electrostatics.field-potential): motion of a charged particle in a uniform electric field (F = qE, a = qE/m, deflection between plates) is not named.
changes.change: Added the motion of a charged particle in a uniform electric field; magnetic-force.moving-charge now sends a charge in an electric field alone here.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, opus finding (too-narrow, refraction.laws): which wave quantities change and which stay constant (frequency) on crossing media is implied, not named, and could be read under waves.properties or waves.equation.
changes.change: Named which of speed, wavelength and frequency change on crossing a boundary, with a rule that this goes to refraction.laws for any wave; waves.properties now points there. waves.equation already sends calculations that need a refractive index to that subtopic.

changes.evidence: Matchtest UTME, opus finding (misplaced, fluids.atmospheric): the manometer measures gas pressure, not atmospheric pressure, yet sits only under fluids.atmospheric, and gas pressure measurement has no clear single home.
changes.change: Renamed to 'Atmospheric pressure and measuring pressure' (id kept) and named the manometer as the gauge for a gas supply's pressure against atmospheric pressure, with a rule sending pressure changing with volume or temperature to gas-laws. The legacy 'Pressure in gases' stays on the gas-laws parent because it spans both topics; the legacy note now says its manometer questions belong to fluids.atmospheric.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC 2021 Q42 disagreement ('not a characteristic of a plane progressive wave', sonnet waves.production, opus waves.progressive); sonnet finding (overlap, waves.production / waves.superposition); opus finding (overlap, waves.progressive): the defining features of a progressive wave have no home.
changes.change: waves.progressive is renamed 'Progressive waves: features, equation and phase difference' (id kept) and now holds the defining features, including which statement is or is not one. waves.production, waves.types and waves.superposition each gained a rule sending those features to waves.progressive; stationary-wave features stay in waves.superposition.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC 2022 Q45 disagreement (50 g object released, sonnet motion.free-fall, opus energy.pe-ke); opus finding (overlap, motion.free-fall).
changes.change: Both covers lines now say: the speed of a body dropped or thrown vertically, when only a speed, height or time is asked, goes to motion.free-fall even when its mass is given; it goes to energy.pe-ke when an energy is asked or the path is a slope, curve or pendulum.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, sonnet finding (overlap, fluids.liquid-pressure / fluids.atmospheric) and opus finding (overlap, fluids.liquid-pressure): total pressure at a depth from a barometer reading plus h rho g has no rule.
changes.change: Both covers lines now send the total pressure at a depth, even when it starts from a barometer reading, to fluids.liquid-pressure; fluids.atmospheric also names converting a mercury-column reading to pascals.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, sonnet finding (missing, electric-cells.types / electric-cells.emf-internal) and opus finding (overlap, electric-cells.types): what does and does not determine a cell's e.m.f. is named by neither.
changes.change: electric-cells.emf-internal now names what does and does not set a cell's e.m.f. (the materials of its plates and electrolyte, not its size); electric-cells.types has a rule sending that question there.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, sonnet finding (missing, atom.models / nucleus.composition) and opus finding (overlap, atom.models): a neutral atom having equal numbers of protons and electrons, and counts of protons, electrons and neutrons, have no home.
changes.change: nucleus.composition now names the electron count of a neutral atom (equal to Z) and counting all three particles from nuclide notation; atom.models sends these to nucleus.composition, and nucleus.composition sends models back.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, sonnet finding (overlap, energy.forms-conservation / magnetic-force.motor): a bare energy-conversion fact about a motor fits both.
changes.change: Both covers lines now say the energy change in a device goes to energy.forms-conservation even when the device has its own subtopic, and how the device works goes to that subtopic. The existing exception for the energy a cell stores (electric-cells.types) is kept.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, opus finding (overlap, dispersion.spectrum): the order of wavelength among the visible colours has no rule.
changes.change: dispersion.spectrum now names the order of the colours by wavelength and frequency; both covers lines send order within the visible band to dispersion.spectrum and order across bands to em-waves.spectrum.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, opus finding (overlap, current-electricity.meters): the galvanometer is split, with sensitivity in meters and the coil in magnetic-force.motor; why more turns raise sensitivity needs both.
changes.change: Moved galvanometer sensitivity out of current-electricity.meters into magnetic-force.motor with its construction; both covers lines say construction and sensitivity go to magnetic-force.motor, and choosing, connecting and converting meters stay in current-electricity.meters.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, opus finding (overlap, measurement.dimensions): two rules collide on expressing a named unit in base units (the joule as kg m^2 s^-2).
changes.change: Both covers lines now say a unit written in base units or in M, L and T goes to measurement.dimensions whatever topic the quantity belongs to; naming a unit such as the tesla still goes to the quantity's own subtopic.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, opus finding (too-narrow, capacitors.capacitance): capacitor behaviour in a circuit (blocking d.c., passing or filtering a.c., charging and discharging) is named nowhere.
changes.change: Added charging and discharging, blocking d.c. while passing a.c., and smoothing and filtering, with a rule in both capacitors.capacitance and ac-circuits.reactance that reactance calculations and phase go to ac-circuits.reactance.

changes.evidence: Matchtest WAEC, opus finding (overlap, nucleus.radiations): deflection of alpha, beta and gamma in a magnetic or electric field could be read as magnetic-force.moving-charge.
changes.change: nucleus.radiations now names their deflection in fields; it, magnetic-force.moving-charge and electrostatics.field-potential all send that question to nucleus.radiations.

not_changed.finding: Coverage, WASSCE 5(b) note: heart-beat and sand-clock are not named.
not_changed.reason: The coverage map marks the item covered: they fall under the time-measuring devices already in measurement.instruments, and no placement split on them.

Kept. Its covers line already says why it exists: WAEC Paper 3, the practical paper, sets a graph of results with its gradient and intercept, and the legacy topic Graph slope interpretation holds such questions. Merging it would scatter those questions.
Kept. Its covers line already says a real paper tests it (WAEC 2025 Q40) and that the legacy topics Bernoulli's principle and Streamline vs turbulent flow fold into it.
